ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that in an equilateral triangle $ABC$, $D$ is the midpoint of $AC$, $E$ is a point on the extension line of $BC$, and $CD = CE$, $M$ is the midpoint of $BE$. What is the measure of $\angle E$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle, \\
$\therefore \angle ACB=60^\circ$, \\
since $CD=CE$, \\
$\therefore \angle CDE=\angle E$, \\
Also, since $\angle ACB=\angle CDE+\angle E$, \\
$\therefore \angle E=\boxed{30^\circ}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows a triangle ABC, with A above, B at the lower left, C on the base, and BC extended to the right to E; D is located on side AC, and D, C, A are collinear; line segment DE connects to point E on the right, M is on BE and is connected to D by a vertical line segment, but M is not needed when finding angle E. It can be seen in the figure that E is on the extension of BC, therefore B, C, E are collinear. Then reason: Because ABC is an equilateral triangle, ∠ACB=60°. Since D is on AC, ray CD is in the same direction as CA; since E is on the extension of BC, ray CE is in the opposite direction to CB. Therefore in triangle DCE, ∠ACB is the exterior angle at point C, satisfying ∠ACB=∠CDE+∠DEC. Also, from the given CD=CE, triangle DCE is an isosceles triangle, so the base angles ∠CDE=∠DEC, that is, ∠CDE=∠E. Thus 60°=∠CDE+∠E=2∠E, so ∠E=30°.
